sam.sample@example.ac.uk · 07700 900456
EDUCATION
PhD Computational Biology, Northfield University Oct 2021 – present
MSc Bioinformatics, Northfield University 2019 – 2021
RESEARCH EXPERIENCE
Research Assistant, Genome Lab 03/2018 – 09/2018

Sample, S. and Example, A. (2024). A method for aligning long reads. Journal of Examples, 12(3), 45–67.

CONFERENCES AND TALKS
• Presented a poster on long-read alignment at the Example Genomics Meeting, 2023.
SKILLS
Python, R, Bash, Nextflow

findings.explanation: EDUCATION runs most recent first, as far as the dates show. One pair of entries overlaps, which is fine: people often hold two roles at once, and an employer's dates can contain the roles within it. Work and study are compared separately, so studying while working is never counted against you.
We found no first-person pronouns in your bullet points.
Months are shortened on 1 line and in numbers on 1 line. In EDUCATION, 2 entries give months and 1 gives only years.
findings.action: Pick one way of writing dates and use it throughout. Either is fine, as long as it's the same.

findings.explanation: Your 4 bullets end the same way and have no doubled punctuation. This covers punctuation at the ends of bullets, not punctuation inside sentences.
Your 4 bullets start the same way and use one symbol, as far as the text shows. Where a line had no symbol in the text, we didn't count that as a difference, because reading a file can lose them.
Your 3 section headings use the same capitalisation and punctuation. This covers the words of the headings only, not their size or style on the page.
We didn't assess fonts, font sizes, alignment, spacing or colour. These checks read the text of your CV, not how the page looks, so we can't say whether they are consistent.
findings.action: Check these by eye, or ask your careers adviser to look at the page.
